newsitem.title: JAPAN: GDP data shows Japan economy getting firmer--MOF.
newsitem.headline: GDP data shows Japan economy getting firmer--MOF.

text.p: Latest gross domestic product (GDP) data shows Japan's economy is getting firmer, led by steady private demand, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
"The GDP figures show that the foothold of Japan's economy is becoming firmer, guided by steady private demand," Ogawa said.
He said the economy was likely to achieve the government's target of 2.5 percent growth for the current fiscal year ending on March 31.

Ogawa added that although growth may slow at the start of the new fiscal year, which begins on April 1, the economy was likely to resume growth and reach the government's target of 1.9 percent for the 1997/98 fiscal year.
Asked about a recent fall in public works spending, Ogawa said a rise in private demand would more than offset that fall.
